arch.title: Architecture
arch.subtitle: Clean Architecture that is verified, not declared
arch.text: Four projects whose dependencies always point towards the domain. Below, the real trace of the calls this interface makes to the API.
arch.layer.domain: Entities, invariants and the state machine. It references no external package: no EF Core, no ASP.NET, not even dependency injection.
arch.layer.application: Use cases, DTOs and persistence contracts. It orchestrates aggregates and decides the transaction boundary, but does not know which engine lies underneath.
arch.layer.infrastructure: EF Core, SQLite, Fluent API configuration and read queries. It implements the interfaces Application declares: the dependency points inwards.
arch.layer.api: REST controllers, the RFC 7807 error contract, rate limiting and this very interface, served as static files from the same origin.

arch.machine.title: State machine
arch.decisions.title: Technical decisions
arch.decisions.hint: Why the code is the way it is, not just what it does
arch.decision.money.title: Money is stored in integer cents
arch.decision.money.text: SQLite has no decimal type and EF Core would persist it as text, so ORDER BY and SUM would work on strings. An INTEGER converter makes ordering and aggregation exact, and removes floating-point error in amounts.
arch.decision.concurrency.title: Optimistic concurrency on stock
arch.decision.concurrency.text: Product carries a version token. If two requests try to reserve the last unit at once, the second fails on the UPDATE and gets a 409 instead of overselling.
arch.decision.uow.title: Explicit unit of work
arch.decision.uow.text: Repositories no longer commit on their own. Adding a line touches two aggregates — order and product — and both are persisted in the same transaction, or neither.
arch.decision.totals.title: Order totals are materialised
arch.decision.totals.text: They are recalculated on every basket change instead of derived on read, so lists and metrics aggregate in the database without loading each order's lines.
arch.decision.errors.title: Errors as a contract, not text
arch.decision.errors.text: A single handler translates every exception into ProblemDetails with a stable code. A business failure is 4xx and a technical failure stays 500, never the reverse.
arch.decision.holds.title: Holds that expire
arch.decision.holds.text: A drop owns its units. An unconfirmed hold returns its own when it expires, and the clock is applied on every read: a stopped process never leaves stock locked.
